title: Shorts Creators Keep Just 45% of Ad Money
description:
How much does a YouTuber get paid for a million views?

Sources:
- YouTube Blog: YouTube Partner Program, Explained (Feb 2025): https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/youtube-partner-program-explained/
- YouTube Help: YouTube Partner Program overview and eligibility: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72857
- YouTube Help: Shorts monetization policies and Creator Pool example: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12504220

Share percentages and requirements are from YouTube's own pages; the $405 figure is YouTube's hypothetical Creator Pool example, not a guaranteed rate. Not financial advice.

#shorts #youtube #creators #howtheymakemoney

loop: So next time you watch a Short, ask yourself:

scenes.narration: How much does a YouTuber get paid for a million views?
First, you have to get in. YouTube's Partner Program needs 1,000 subscribers.

visual.label: subscribers to join YouTube's Partner Program

scenes.narration: Plus 4,000 watch hours in a year, or 10 million Shorts views in 90 days.
Then the ads pay. On long videos, creators keep 55 percent of the ad money.

visual.label: creators' share of ad revenue, long videos

scenes.narration: On Shorts, ad money is pooled, and creators keep 45 percent of their share.
In a made-up example from YouTube, a Short with 1 million views earned 405 dollars.
